newsitem.title: USA: Judge in Simpson trial announces juror's dismissal.
newsitem.headline: Judge in Simpson trial announces juror's dismissal.

text.p: The judge in the O.J. Simpson civil trial announced on Tuesday he had dismissed a juror for misconduct.

At the start of the day's court session, Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki told the remaining jurors he had decided to remove the woman from the panel, saying, "the juror has conducted herself in a way inappropriate for a juror sitting on the case."
The judge said the juror's offence involved "communicating with or attempting to communicate with persons connected with this case," but he gave no further details.

Fujisaki make his decision Monday to dismiss the woman, who appears to be in her late 20s and works in retail jewelry sales. She has been variously described in news reports as white, Hispanic and of mixed white and Hispanic heritage.

The woman told Los Angeles TV station KABC Tuesday that the closest she came to contact was making a comment about a law clerk's tie. "I said, I like his tie...,'" she said. "This is an absolutely ludicrous reason for being dismissed."

An alternate juror was selected to replace her. It marked the first departure of a regular juror since a panellist was booted off the case because of a drinking problem immediately after the jury was seated in October. An alternate woman juror was dismissed in mid-November after attorneys complained that she had dozed off during trial testimony.
